newsitem.title: USA: CSX says intends to proceed with tender.
newsitem.headline: CSX says intends to proceed with tender.

text.p: CSX Corp said it intended to proceed with its tender offer for 19.9 percent of the shares in Conrail Inc, following a federal appeals court decision on the case.
"We intend to proceed with our tender offer as planned," a CSX spokesman told Reuters. The $110 per share offer expires at midnight Eastern time tonight.

A panel of the Third U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Wednesday denied a request by Norfolk Southern Corp for an emergency injunction to block CSX's offer pending an appeal of a lower court ruling also refusing to block the offer.
But the appeals court said it would consider taking an expedited appeal.

Takeover stock traders said the ruling raises the possibility that a later appeals court decision could prevent CSX from voting the shares, or otherwise interfere with the merger and leave CSX holding some $2 billion worth of Conrail stock.
"They must feel the case is so strong that there is no risk that they (the appeals court judges) do anything draconian later," said an arbitrageur.

CSX and Conrail said in a joint statement on the decision, "We are pleased that the U.S. Court of Appeals has let stand yesterday's District Court ruling. Despite Norfolk Southern's continuing attempts to derail the merger of Conrail and CSX, we are committed to each other and to the great future of our combined companies."
